minutes.headline: Committee reviewed the design-services RFP but lost its quorum mid-review and adjourned with no vote.
minutes.summary: The Municipal Building Design Committee met for the first time since last November and walked through the draft RFP for design services for a new town hall, the Ritter building and the existing town hall. Members discussed competitive pricing, meeting frequency, soil borings, cost-estimate review and site-plan scope. The meeting reached the quality requirements section, then lost its quorum and adjourned without a motion. The chair will email the revised RFP and ask members to review section three.

attendees.name_as_heard: Mrs scullen Brey / Mr skull bini (Tony)

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none was offered.
Asked what happens to the town clerk's second office and storage planned for TCP. Said she does not favor spending money on TCP and wants the plan run past the select board and the public.
Asked where money would come from to relocate Ritter offices into TCP before renovation. Said TCP is only partly occupied and has a damaged hallway roof. Said the RFP does not budget for the moves.

budget_items.what_was_said: The committee has an ARPA allocation for the design work. A rule change over the summer requires the funds to be under contract by year end, so the select board wants contracts by October.
The figure came from an architectural team's estimate, with an escalator added for wiggle room. It was not set by the committee as a group.

budget_items.topic: Estimated construction cost in the RFP
budget_items.what_was_said: The draft states one construction estimate. The chair thinks the real figure is lower, and the town manager wants costs kept down.
The RFP notes the Ritter building was built for book storage, which affects pricing because floor loading is higher than for an office.
Evening meetings drive up a design contract's price. Members discussed reducing the meeting count or letting the bidder price it.
Soil borings could use up a large share of the design money, though an exotic foundation could add major cost. Members agreed to drop them from this phase.
A member said the RFP's required experience range is too low given the project size and should be raised.
A resident cited the earlier TCP estimate. She said she opposes putting money into TCP.
A speaker said the cost of moving offices into TCP is not in the RFP request.

decisions.decision: Reduce the number of paper copies required to three and add a requirement for a digital copy.
Remove the soil borings and subsurface investigation requirement from this phase's deliverables, with the committee in agreement.
TCP stays the voting location and holds the town clerk's voting equipment for now. The chair will make a note on town clerk storage.
The chair will email the RFP with the notes so far and ask members to review the quality requirements section before the next meeting.
The meeting adjourned without a motion because it had lost its quorum.

why_it_matters: The RFP covers design work for a new town hall, the Ritter building and the existing town hall, and it is paid from ARPA money that has a contracting deadline, so a stalled review leaves less time before the funds must be under contract.
A resident noted that the cost of moving Ritter offices into TCP is not in the RFP request, so that cost is not yet in any figure for the project.
